details: Bitcoin demonstrated resilience during the ongoing 2026 Iran War, quickly recovering after an initial dip. While traditional safe havens like gold and the US dollar saw predictable reactions, Bitcoin's quick rebound challenges its traditional classification as a pure risk asset. Market participants appear to view the current geopolitical tensions as having a limited effect on Bitcoin's near-term performance, with confidence in its stability.
title: Bitcoin Shows Resilience Amidst Middle East Tensions

details: The U.S. Department of Defense has redefined Bitcoin's role as a national security asset amidst rising global tensions with Russia and China. This repositioning is part of a broader strategy to leverage Bitcoin for power projection, reflecting growing confidence in its strategic importance. This development could potentially drive increased institutional demand and adoption for Bitcoin.
title: US Redefines Bitcoin as National Security Asset Amid Global Tensions

details: North Korean hackers are reportedly responsible for 76% of all cryptocurrency stolen in 2026, with these significant funds being used to finance the regime. This highlights the ongoing cybersecurity risks inherent in the crypto space and the persistent use of digital assets for illicit purposes by state-sponsored actors, often employing advanced techniques like AI for more sophisticated attacks.
title: North Korea Accounts for 76% of Stolen Crypto in 2026

details: Ethereum has seen a breakout from its recent downtrend, as global conflicts impact energy prices and lead traders to shift interest away from traditional assets. Digital assets are increasingly perceived as relatively isolated from the volatility of crude oil and natural gas price hikes. Additionally, higher energy costs for crypto mining can temporarily restrict supply, contributing to a boost in cryptocurrency prices.
title: Ethereum Breaks Out as Traders Shift from Traditional Assets
